Title: Baked Salmon with Fresh Lemon and Dill
Ingredients: 4 salmon fillets (6 oz each) | 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil | 1 fresh lemon, sliced into thin wheels | 2 tbsp fresh dill, chopped | Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper to taste
Instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Line rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. 2. Arrange salmon fillets on baking sheet skin-side down. 3. Drizzle fillets evenly with olive oil; season with salt and black pepper. 4. Top each fillet with fresh lemon slices and generous sprigs of chopped fresh dill. 5. Bake in preheated oven for 15 to 20 minutes until salmon flakes easily with a fork and internal temperature reaches 145°F. 6. Serve warm with pan juices.
Source: 7 Nutrient-Packed Recipes That Make Healthy Eating a Breeze - Prime Women (Section: Baked Salmon with Lemon and Dill)
Notes: Oven temperature & doneness: Source specifies 375°F (190°C) baking for 15-20 minutes until fish flakes easily with a fork, satisfying the FDA fin fish safety requirement of 145°F (63°C).

Title: Sheet-Pan Chili-Lemon Salmon and Potatoes
Ingredients: 4 center-cut salmon fillets (6 oz each) | 1 lb baby Yukon gold potatoes, halved | 1 bunch asparagus, trimmed | 2 tbsp olive oil | 1 tsp chili powder | 1/2 tsp cumin | 1/2 tsp garlic powder | 1 tbsp lemon juice | Salt and pepper to taste
Instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 400°F (204°C). 2. Toss halved potatoes with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper on large baking sheet. Roast 15 minutes. 3. Push potatoes to side, add salmon fillets and asparagus to center of sheet pan. 4. Whisk remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and lemon juice; brush over salmon and asparagus. 5. Return sheet pan to oven and roast 10-12 minutes until salmon registers 145°F and flakes easily and potatoes are fork-tender. 6. Serve directly from sheet pan.
Source: Healthy Weeknight Dinners You'll Actually Crave - Dishing Out Health (Section: Sheet Pan Chili-Lemon Salmon)
Notes: Staggered roasting: Potatoes roast for 15 minutes first, then salmon and vegetables are added for 10-12 minutes at 400°F to prevent delicate fish from drying out while ensuring 145°F doneness.

Title: Skillet Salmon with Creamy Spinach and Artichokes
Ingredients: 4 skin-on salmon fillets (6 oz each) | 1 tbsp olive oil | 1 can (14 oz) artichoke hearts, drained and chopped | 3 cups baby spinach | 2 cloves garlic, minced | 1/2 cup low-sodium vegetable broth | 1/3 cup heavy cream or coconut cream | 1/4 cup grated Parmesan | Salt and pepper to taste
Instructions: 1. Season salmon fillets with salt and pepper. 2. Heat olive oil in large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. 3. Add salmon skin-side down; sear 4-5 minutes until skin is crisp. Flip and cook 3 minutes until internal temperature hits 140°F-145°F; transfer to plate. 4. Reduce heat to medium, add minced garlic and chopped artichoke hearts; sauté 2 minutes. 5. Pour in broth and cream; simmer 3 minutes. Stir in spinach and Parmesan until spinach wilts. 6. Nestle seared salmon back into creamy skillet sauce and serve immediately.
Source: Healthy Weeknight Dinners You'll Actually Crave - Dishing Out Health (Section: Spinach Artichoke Salmon Skillet)
Notes: Pan-searing temperature: Skin-side down searing for 4-5 minutes creates crispy skin barrier before 3-minute flip to finish at 145°F.

Title: Classic Miso-Glazed Broiled Salmon
Ingredients: 4 salmon fillets (6 oz each) | 3 tbsp white miso paste | 2 tbsp mirin | 1 tbsp soy sauce | 1 tbsp brown sugar | 1 tsp grated fresh ginger | 1 tsp toasted sesame oil | Sliced scallions for garnish
Instructions: 1. Whisk white miso, mirin, soy sauce, brown sugar, grated ginger, and sesame oil in small bowl until smooth. 2. Place salmon fillets on foil-lined baking sheet sprayed with oil; brush miso glaze generously over tops. 3. Set oven broiler to HIGH with rack positioned 5-6 inches from heating element. 4. Broil salmon for 6 to 8 minutes, watching carefully so miso glaze caramelizes into dark spots without burning. 5. Confirm internal temperature reaches 145°F and flesh flakes under light pressure. Garnish with scallions.
Source: Recipes - The Nutrition Source | Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health (Section: Heart-Healthy Fish)
Notes: Broiler watch: Sugars in miso caramelize rapidly under high broil (6-8 minutes); rack must be positioned 5-6 inches away to cook through to 145°F without scorching.

Title: Crispy Skin Pan-Roasted Salmon with Lemon & Capers
Ingredients: 2 skin-on salmon fillets (6 oz each) | 1 tbsp olive oil | 1 tbsp unsalted butter | 1 tbsp capers, drained | 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice | 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley | Salt and pepper to taste
Instructions: 1. Thoroughly dry salmon skin with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and pepper. 2. Heat olive oil in stainless or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. 3. Place fillets skin-side down, pressing gently with spatula for 10 seconds to prevent curling. 4. Cook undisturbed 5 minutes until skin is golden-crisp and flesh is cooked 3/4 way up. 5. Flip fillets, add butter, capers, and lemon juice. Cook 2-3 minutes while spooning pan juices over fish until internal temperature reaches 145°F. 6. Garnish with parsley and serve.
Source: Recipes - The Nutrition Source | Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health (Section: Seafood Dinners)
Notes: Heat ratio: 70% of cooking occurs on skin side (5 minutes) to insulate delicate flesh and crisp skin, flipping for only 2-3 minutes to reach 145°F.

Title: Honey-Mustard Glazed Baked Salmon
Protein Cut: Salmon fillets or whole salmon side
Ingredients: 4 salmon fillets (6 oz each) | 2 tbsp Dijon mustard | 1 tbsp whole-grain mustard | 2 tbsp honey | 1 clove garlic, minced | 1 tbsp olive oil | 1/2 tsp smoked paprika | Salt and pepper
Instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 400°F (204°C). Line baking sheet with foil. 2. Whisk Dijon mustard, whole-grain mustard, honey, minced garlic, olive oil, and paprika in small bowl. 3. Place salmon fillets skin-side down on sheet; season lightly with salt and pepper. 4. Spoon honey-mustard glaze over fillets. 5. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until salmon flakes with fork and registers 145°F in thickest portion. 6. Serve immediately.
Source: 45 Healthy Comfort Food Recipes That Are Packed with Flavor - Food Network (Section: Healthy Seafood Mains)
Notes: Glaze caramelization: 400°F bake time of 12-14 minutes balances glaze setting with 145°F internal temperature.

Title: Cast-Iron Blackened Cajun Salmon
Ingredients: 4 thick skinless salmon fillets (6 oz each) | 2 tbsp Cajun seasoning blend (paprika, cayenne, garlic, onion, thyme, oregano) | 2 tbsp melted butter | Lemon wedges for serving
Instructions: 1. Heat dry cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking hot. 2. Dip salmon fillets in melted butter, then dredge both sides in Cajun seasoning blend. 3. Lay seasoned fillets in smoking hot skillet. Cook 3 to 4 minutes without moving until spice crust turns deeply blackened. 4. Carefully flip and cook 3 minutes on second side until internal temperature registers 145°F. 5. Remove immediately and serve with fresh lemon wedges.
Source: Our 50 Most-Popular Healthy Recipes - Food Network (Section: Most Saved Seafood)
Notes: Blackening safety: Requires smoking-hot skillet and 3-4 minutes per side. Butter-spice coating chars quickly while interior gently steams to 145°F.
